speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly what happens when you wake up frightened, and does anyone else in the family have similar experiences?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you ever have sudden bursts of intense fear or panic while falling asleep or during the night, where you feel unable to move or speak? REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography; REQUEST IMAGES: EEG_sleep_study.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The patient's sleep diary reveals a pattern correlating with the described episodes, with noted disturbances occurring 1-2 times a week. Polysomnography findings indicate it is not indicated at this stage based on history and normal physical examination. EEG_sleep_study was not performed as Polysomnography was not indicated.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.
